model_output.score_comment_short: Recent project sizes and delivery results make the project management work easy to place.
model_output.score_comment_long: The current role gives project values, concurrent workload, trade counts, and delivery results. It says less about how you handled scheduling, buyout, and change orders. Add a concrete example to the most important bullets.
model_output.score_plain: Your recent experience gives a reviewer useful facts to compare with a construction project management opening. A few details about your decisions would make the results easier to assess.
model_output.first_impression: You present a clear commercial construction project management background, with tenant improvements and ground-up retail both named. The current role is specific about project value and workload, though the methods behind its results are brief.
model_output.biggest_gap_example: "Built the three-week look-ahead schedule with superintendents" does not explain what you contributed to the schedule or how it was used on site.
model_output.summary: Delivering a $14M grocery store build 3 weeks ahead of schedule in 2024 is worth keeping because it gives a reviewer a concrete project and delivery result. Your current Project Manager role also shows responsibility for concurrent tenant improvements, trade buyout, and change orders. Earlier work on submittals, RFIs, and look-ahead scheduling connects naturally to that role. The resume doesn't yet explain which scheduling or coordination choices contributed to the grocery store delivery, so a reviewer has less to work with when assessing how you achieved it.
strengths: The 4 to 6 concurrent tenant-improvement projects, worth $1M to $8M each, make your current workload tangible.
Managing bids and buyout for 20 to 30 trades per project shows the breadth of subcontractor coordination.
The $5M to $20M office and retail projects give your earlier submittal and RFI work useful context.
gaps: The change-order result doesn't explain how you kept orders under 3% of contract value, leaving the approach behind that figure unclear.
The buyout bullet doesn't say what you evaluated or decided during subcontractor selection, which limits the picture of your purchasing work.
Your skills list names Procore, Bluebeam, and MS Project but doesn't connect them to particular project tasks, making their use difficult to assess.
